newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crude dumps June ahead of Tuesday expiry.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crude dumps June ahead of Tuesday expiry.

text.p: Domestic cash crude prices sunk Monday for spot June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, reflecting bearish sentiment ahead of Tuesday's expiry.
June WTI/Cushing was talked around 50 cents weaker late in the day at $21.45-55 a barrel, but dropped more dramatically against July WTI/Cushing.
June/July spreads edged to minus 40 cents, pushing Postings prices to trade at $1.75, 30 cents lower than Friday.
Traders said the negative June performance came not only on technical consolidation, but on fundamentals ahead of June NYMEX expiration and Friday pipeline scheduling deadlines.

"No significant player will be taking delivery of June WTI, in essence it is valueless. Tanks in Cushing are full, Brent-WTI has been kept wide and PADD II inventories are high," said a trader in Texas.
Exchange for Physical (EFPs) deals, which allow a buyer or seller to swap a futures for a physical position, were heard traded to 25 cents on Monday in a panicky market.

EFPs act as an insurance policy against getting stuck with foreign crude delivered against NYMEX, an unsual event, but a situation that appeared in May as a result of market economics and tight supplies from an unruly Nigerian market.

For June, traders eyed a possible delivery of some 1-1.5 million barrels of foreign barrels into NYMEX, some of which would be re-delivered barrels from May when 2.73 million barrels of foreigns were delivered into NYMEX.
Market economics dictate that a company that receives Bonny Light instead of WTI, would receive a fixed discount of 60 cents per barrel to compensate for the differing crude qualities.
For the grades on Monday, Midland sweet barrels sold weaker at 40 cents under June WTI/Cushing, and Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James moved between 3-7 cents under marker.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire sold at a solid 72 cents discount to June benchmark, steady from late talk Friday.
West Texas Sour/Midland and Eugene Island advanced, notably for Eugene Island which gained on the closure of Texaco's Eugene Island pipeline due to a leak.
The company expects 120,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude to be shut in until Thursday at the earliest following a crack on part of its Eugene Island pipeline, which caused a spill into Lake Barre.
Deals were sealed for Eugene barrels some 20 cents firmer than late Friday around a discount of $1.40 to benchmark.
Later in the session, Eugene Island retreated to talk around $1.50-45 below June WTI/Cushing.
